title: Final consonants (batchim)
summary: A consonant written under the vowel closes the syllable.
explanation: A syllable block can end in a consonant, written at the bottom of the block. This final consonant is called batchim (받침).
Read a block in this order: first consonant, vowel, then the batchim. 한 is ㅎ + ㅏ + ㄴ.
A final consonant is not released: your mouth closes on the sound and stops. Final ㄱ, ㄷ and ㅂ are cut short, with no burst of air.
Some blocks have two consonants at the bottom. Before a pause or another consonant only one of them is pronounced.

title: The seven final sounds
summary: Many letters can be written as batchim, but only seven sounds are heard.
explanation: At the end of a syllable only seven sounds exist: ㄱ, ㄴ, ㄷ, ㄹ, ㅁ, ㅂ and ㅇ.
ㄱ, ㅋ and ㄲ all sound like ㄱ. ㅂ and ㅍ both sound like ㅂ.
ㄷ, ㅌ, ㅅ, ㅆ, ㅈ, ㅊ and ㅎ all sound like ㄷ.
This applies when the syllable is followed by a pause or by a consonant. Before a vowel, the linking rule applies instead.

title: Linking
summary: A final consonant moves over to a following vowel.
explanation: When a syllable ends in a consonant and the next syllable starts with the silent ㅇ, the consonant is pronounced as the start of the next syllable.
The spelling does not change. Only the pronunciation moves.
With a double batchim, the first consonant stays and the second one moves over.
Final ㅇ (ng) does not move, and final ㅎ is silent before a vowel.

title: Nasalization
summary: ㄱ, ㄷ and ㅂ sounds become nasal before ㄴ or ㅁ.
explanation: When a final ㄱ, ㄷ or ㅂ sound is followed by ㄴ or ㅁ, it changes into the matching nasal sound.
ㄱ becomes ㅇ (ng), ㄷ becomes ㄴ, and ㅂ becomes ㅁ.
This is why the very common ending 입니다 is pronounced 임니다.

title: Tensing
summary: A soft consonant becomes tense after a final ㄱ, ㄷ or ㅂ sound.
explanation: After a final ㄱ, ㄷ or ㅂ sound, the next ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ, ㅅ or ㅈ is pronounced as its tense partner.
ㄱ becomes ㄲ, ㄷ becomes ㄸ, ㅂ becomes ㅃ, ㅅ becomes ㅆ, and ㅈ becomes ㅉ.
The spelling stays the same.

title: Aspiration with ㅎ
summary: ㅎ merges with ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ or ㅈ into ㅋ, ㅌ, ㅍ or ㅊ.
explanation: When ㅎ meets ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ or ㅈ, in either order, the two merge into one aspirated sound.
ㄱ becomes ㅋ, ㄷ becomes ㅌ, ㅂ becomes ㅍ, and ㅈ becomes ㅊ.
Before a vowel, final ㅎ is simply silent: 좋아요 is pronounced 조아요.

title: ㄷ and ㅌ before 이
summary: Final ㄷ or ㅌ before 이 sounds like ㅈ or ㅊ: 같이 is said 가치.
explanation: When a syllable ends in ㄷ or ㅌ and the next syllable is 이, the consonant moves over and changes: ㄷ becomes ㅈ, and ㅌ becomes ㅊ.
It happens when the 이 is an ending or a particle added to a word (같 + 이, 끝 + 이), so you meet it all the time in 같이 and in nouns that end in ㅌ.
ㄷ followed by 히 also becomes 치: 닫히다 is said 다치다.
The spelling does not change. Only the pronunciation moves.
